text:
maya: 🚨 ap-southeast-1 GPU nodepool at 100% — cluster-autoscaler is thrashing and several inference pods are Pending with 'Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu'. Noticing a spike of short-lived realtime-batch jobs. Can someone triage?

devon: On it. Can you paste `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and CA events? Also which nodepool is affected (name)?

maya: Affected nodepool = gpu-realtime-prod. Quick dumps: 
```
kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-realtime-prod
ip-10-0-5-1   Ready   12d   v1.24.10   192.0.2.5   gpu-realtime-prod   gpu:1
ip-10-0-5-2   Ready   11d   v1.24.10   192.0.2.6   gpu-realtime-prod   gpu:1
... (total 6 nodes, all at 100% alloc)
```
and CA events tail:
```
I0503 14:12:31 cluster-autoscaler: Scale-up: ignoring 3/8 unneeded because of pending pods
I0503 14:12:45 cluster-autoscaler: Failed to scale up: max nodes reached for nodegroup gpu-realtime-prod
I0503 14:13:12 cluster-autoscaler: Scale up request triggered for gpu-realtime-prod but integration timed out
```
Pods pending sample:
```
NAME                                  READY STATUS  RESTARTS   AGE
realtime-batch-xx-7qk2               0/1   Pending 0          2m  (Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu)
realtime-batch-yy-4f3r               0/1   Pending 0          1m  (Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu)
```

maya: Also seeing one large training job (gpu-longtrain-prod) stuck in CrashLoopBackOff but still occupying a GPU daemonset pod on a different pool — could be contributing to fragmentation.

lina: Immediate mitigations: 1) cordon/evict low-priority realtime-batch pods (they're stateless), 2) spin up a temporary fallback nodepool with cheaper on-demand A10G nodes and taint it so only pods with toleration can land, 3) increase cluster-autoscaler max for gpu-realtime-prod temporarily if commit allows. We should avoid full cluster-wide scale increase due to cost.

devon: Started cordon on a couple of nodes with a lot of short jobs and issued selective evict for pods with priorityClassName=realtime-burst: 
```
kubectl get pods -n infra -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PRIORITY:.spec.priorityClassName | grep realtime-burst
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-5-2
kubectl delete pod realtime-batch-xx-7qk2 -n ml-realtime --grace-period=10
```
Result: ~8 pending pods rescheduled across remaining nodes but still 12 pending overall.

ops-bot: [automated] Created nodepool gpu-fallback-on-demand (3 nodes, A10G). Provisioning started. ETA ~4m.

maya: pods started to schedule onto gpu-fallback-on-demand but CA still logs "max nodes reached" for gpu-realtime-prod (we didn't bump limit). Some jobs get scattered and cause increased startup latency.

sre-oncall: I'll approve a temporary bump of maxNodes for gpu-realtime-prod from 6 -> 12 for 2 hours to let the backlog clear. Also immediate followups: enforce pod-level resource limits and QoS for realtime-batch, add admission webhook to prevent pods requesting >1 GPU without review, and create a cron to detect bursty submitters (we need rate limiting at the job-submitter side).

devon: Done — updated autoscaler config and scaled maxNodes to 12. CA accepted the change and scale-up is in progress. Quick check shows fallback pool accepting pods and backlog decreasing.

maya: Confirmed backlog down from ~40 pending -> ~6, critical latency stabilized. Cost note: enabling fallback pool + bump will add ~3-4k USD/day if sustained; ops team to BL and tag.

lina: Postmortem action items: 1) enforce GPU request limits on CI/CD templates, 2) add quota and rate limiting for realtime-batch submitter, 3) make gpu-fallback nodepool autoscaleable with taint+toleration so CA doesn't get blocked by single nodegroup limits, 4) create an incident runbook for 'GPU fragmentation + CA max hit'. I'll open tickets.

devon: I'll also add a short-term admission control that rejects pods without resource.limits.gpu for the next week to prevent regressions.

maya: Thanks all — keeping this thread for the tl;dr and follow-ups. Will attach the SR and billing tags once I have numbers. :wave:
